rooms.evidence: All twelve supplied room/space labels occur at their source locations. PANTRY labels kitchen joinery, not a separate walk-in room; CRAWLSPACE ACCESS labels access beneath the stair.

doorways.evidence: The marked house doors connect the correct spaces, including the WC pocket door into CENTRAL HALL. Two source screen doors are omitted: the west entrance to SUNSET PORCH and the south entrance to BREAKFAST PORCH. Kitchen, dining and hall open-plan circulation must remain open.

stairs.evidence: The main stair approaches from the bottom and ascends upward. Its lower tread run ends at a break adjoining CRAWLSPACE ACCESS; the orange rectangle also covers the under-stair enclosure. The source states 17 R @ 7.7 inches [195], but does not individually number the visible treads or establish an upper landing footprint here. Exterior BRICK STEPS are also drawn.

barriers.evidence: At least one barrier could not be classified against the source.

ceilings.evidence: No ceiling-face, raked-ceiling or ceiling-height annotation is shown. Joist annotations and deck drainage slopes are not ceiling regions.

roof.evidence: No roof plane or roof pitch is shown in these review images; the printed 1–2% slopes refer to decking.

dimensions.evidence: All four scale readings match their bracketed metric dimensions and extension lines: 12600, 8400, 4800 and 3000 mm. Opening sizes agree with the local door/window schedules; their unprinted sill defaults are not source measurements.

outdoor.evidence: STOOP is correctly outside the enclosed house, between the rear door and brick steps. It requires no enclosing walls. Both screened porches and the wrapping FRONT PORCH retain their source entry gaps and outdoor edges.

barriers.evidence: Barrier 0: paired screen-frame lines between 4x4 posts on SUNSET PORCH; no local low-rail label.
Barrier 1: screened perimeter from corner post to screen-door jamb; screen framing does not alone establish a balustrade.
Barrier 2: paired screened-perimeter lines and posts south of the screen entrance; low-rail construction is not specified locally.
Barrier 3: SUNSET PORCH screen/post perimeter; no independent railing-height annotation at this edge.
Barrier 4: BREAKFAST PORCH screened perimeter with posts; screen/frame lines are shown, but a low rail is not separately identified.
Barrier 5: east porch edge is explicitly called out as 30-inch RAILING; the upper portion also bounds the screened porch.
Barrier 6: screen-frame segment between house and screen-door jamb, with a post; no distinct low-wall symbol.
Barrier 7: screen-frame segment east of the screen door, between posts; low-rail detail is not independently legible.
Barrier 8: paired porch-edge rail lines below the east brick-step entrance; continuation of the labelled porch railing.
Barrier 9: source explicitly labels this post-supported edge 30-inch PORCH RAILING.
Barrier 10: paired front-porch rail lines between posts, stopping at the front-step opening; same porch railing construction.
Barrier 11: paired side-return rail lines connect the front corner post to the house-side porch post.
Barrier 12: the stair closeup shows a paired rail and a round newel at its bottom end, not merely aligned tread ends. Retain this rail.

parts.supportEvidence: Door E and CRAWLSPACE ACCESS are drawn beneath the stair; note 4 identifies the closet below the stairs.
parts.stepEvidence: 17 R @ 7.7" [195]. Upper treads are partly obscured by the under-stair closet drawing; the visible run terminates at the hall-side enclosure.

notes: Converted from the Southern Farmhouse 1st and 2nd floor plans (sheets A1.1 and A1.2), scaled from their printed dimensions.
Ceiling heights come from the drawing set. The main roof is simplified to a gable on the upper walls; the porch roofs keep their drawn 2.5:12 slope. Porch screens are shown as low rails.
This is a sample conversion for exploring the layout, not construction documentation.
